lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: One summer evening in Tuscany, an Irishman was stirring pasta... when his phone buzzed.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A number he didn't know. A photo of a gold ring. And six words.

lines.speaker: PATRICK
lines.text: Hi Sméagol... look what we found.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: To understand that message, we need to go back nine days... to a river.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Patrick Mohr, from Dún Laoghaire, near Dublin, was holidaying near Bagni di Lucca with his wife, Joanne, and their three daughters.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The girls were jumping off a boulder, and Dad was catching them.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then one daughter grabbed his hand... and his gold wedding ring slipped off. Sixteen years of marriage, swept away by the current.

lines.speaker: PATRICK
lines.text: I just stood there a little bit paralysed... with instant knowledge it's gone.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: But Joanne didn't freeze. She ran downstream, to three young Italian men she had never met.

lines.speaker: JOANNE
lines.text: Please, can you help us? My husband's wedding ring... it's in the river!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Filippo Palagi, Nicola Malloggi and Edoardo Poggi. They swapped phone numbers... and joked about going on a quest for the ring, like hobbits.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then the joke became a mission. For two days, they searched from kayaks. Nothing.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: So they went under. They tied themselves to boulders with ropes, pulled on masks, and dived into the strongest current.

lines.speaker: EDOARDO
lines.text: Hold the rope! The current is too strong here!

lines.speaker: PATRICK
lines.text: It's not about the gold ring... it's what it means.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Then, deep in the river, Nicola saw something. A tiny glint... in the sand.

lines.speaker: NICOLA
lines.text: Ragazzi! I found it! I found the ring!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Which brings us back to that kitchen... and that text.

lines.speaker: PATRICK
lines.text: Joanne! Girls! They found it!

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: They could have posted it. Instead, they offered to fly it to Ireland themselves, so the family could finish their holiday.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Later, at the family's front door in Dún Laoghaire, there was music. Three young Italians... dressed as hobbits.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: They stayed about a week: Glendalough, a pint of Guinness, dinner with the family. Patrick gave each a silver bracelet engraved with their names.

lines.speaker: FILIPPO
lines.text: Before that, we never knew each other. Now, we have a family in Ireland.

lines.speaker: PATRICK
lines.text: Sometimes you have to put things out into the universe and ask for help. And sometimes, you get an answer.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: A ring is small. So is a "yes" to a stranger. But one small act can turn strangers... into family.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: If this made you smile, share it with someone who needs it today.
